text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE STRAITS TIMES:
- Some teenage offenders will have to do 40 hours of community work in old folks' homes or childcare centres while on probation.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong offers sympathies to families and victims from tour bus crash in Malaysia.
- US military spacecraft detects ice on moon that could resolve debate among scientists about whether there is water on lunar surface.
- Conglomerate Keppel Corp and Britain's Cable and Wireless declare they will bid for second telecom licence to provide local and international telephone services.
- Norwegian industrial group Norsk Hydro ASA and Singapore government investment arm Temasek Holdings establish joint venture to invest in industrial projects in Asia.
- Two businessmen charged in Amcol Holdings case get court nod to travel abroad.
THE BUSINESS TIMES:
- National Computer Board and Singapore CableVision unveil plans for Internet commerce.

- SingaporeConnect, a comprehensive new search service on the Internet, launched by Productivity and Standards Board, National Computer Board and Singapore Press Holdings, will boost globalisation for small and medium-sized enterprises.
- Singapore Regional Index Fund raises Singapore $89 million in just two weeks to top $100 million target by close of launch on December 18.
- Government of Singapore Investment Corp finalise purchase of office block in Sydney's Central Business District for Australia $120 million.
- U.S. dollar hits two-year high against German mark.
- Singapore Airlines deputy chairman and CEO Dr Cheong says deregulation must accompany technological and structural changes in airline industry.
- Poosana Premanoch, director of United Communication Industry group, given post of Thailand's deputy secretary-general to Prime Minister's office.
- Robert Fleming & Co to issue 30 million call warrants of U.S. 10 cents each in Hong Kong Land Holdings at issue price of U.S. 61.2 cents each.
- Far East Levingston Shipbuilding Ltd and Viernamese partner start work on Vietcombank Towers building for u.S. $55 million.
- Scotts Holdings to focus on core competencies.
-- Singapore newsroom 65-8703080
